messages:
maya_cs: Heads-up: Sorrel private VPC cutover scheduled Thu 07:00 PT. Main asks before we start: final CIDR confirmation, IAM role ARNs for provisioning, customer-managed KMS key policy (we need key ARN + policy if they want cross-account access), and where audit logs land (they said GCP SIEM). Any blockers?
cesar_se: thanks. We saw their runbook and a couple items: 1) their current CIDR is 10.12.0.0/16 so we should pick something non-overlapping (propose 10.20.0.0/16). 2) their security insists on explicit kms:Decrypt allow for our service principal + their sec-audit account. Can they paste the desired key policy here?
nikki_net: 10.20.0.0/16 works for us. I attached a quick overlap-check script and a route table diff in the shared S3 bucket (s3://redwood-internal/sorrel/route-diffs/1719504321.txt). Script snippet below for their infra folks to run:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# simple CIDR overlap check (requires cidrcalc)
CIDR_A="10.12.0.0/16"
CIDR_B="$1"
if cidrcalc -o $CIDR_A $CIDR_B | grep -q "overlap"; then
  echo "overlap detected"
  exit 1
fi
echo "no overlap"
```

emma_ops: On audit logs: Sorrel wants logs forwarded to a GCP Pub/Sub endpoint (projects/sorrel-prod/topics/redwood-logs). They also require TLS + JWT bearer for auth. Can Redwood push logs to Pub/Sub, or do we need their forwarder?
cesar_se: we support push to HTTP endpoints and can integrate with a customer push agent for Pub/Sub. If they require JWT bearer, they'll need to give us a service account with a key and IAM role to publish. Alternatively, they can run a lightweight forwarder in their VPC and allow our egress IPs. Which do they prefer?
nikki_net: egress options: we can provide static NAT egress IPs (54.204.88.10/32, 54.204.88.11/32) or they can host a forwarder. If they choose Pub/Sub direct, we need a service account email + pubsub.publisher role.
maya_cs: I'll ask Sorrel for preference. Quick note on KMS: they must include the Redwood service principal arn:aws:iam::888888888888:role/redwood-provisioner in key policy for kms:Encrypt/kms:Decrypt. If they refuse cross-account, we can create a key in their account but need kms:CreateGrant permission during provisioning window.
cesar_se: IAM example (minimal grant) pasted here for their security team:

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowRedwood",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::888888888888:role/redwood-provisioner"},
      "Action": ["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt","kms:CreateGrant","kms:DescribeKey"],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```

emma_ops: Also FYI their compliance team requires 90-day log retention for audit-critical streams. If we route logs into their SIEM we need to ensure no accidental shorter retention on our side. That's a potential renewal risk if compliance isn't met on cutover day.
maya_cs: noted — risk: "audit-retention-mismatch" flagged as medium. If retention <90 days at cutover, CSM to engage renewal ops and propose a remediation plan.
cesar_se: action items: 1) sorrel infra to confirm egress method (pubsub SA vs host forwarder) and provide SA email or forwarder hostname 1: owner: sorrel-ops 1: due: today 18:00 PT. 2) sorrel sec to paste CMK ARN or accept cross-account key policy 1: owner: sorrel-sec 1: due: today 18:00 PT. 3) nikki to post exact NAT egress IPs if they want static allowlist 1: owner: nikki_net 1: due: today 16:00 PT.
nikki_net: posted NAT IPs: [54.204.88.10, 54.204.88.11]. Also uploaded route table and ACL exports to https://redwood-internal.s3.amazonaws.com/sorrel/routes-1719504321.json.
maya_cs: scheduling: dry-run Wed 06:00 PT, cutover Thu 07:00 PT. Will invite sorrel-ops + sorrel-sec + our SRE. Please ensure someone is on-call for 2 hours post-cutover for smoke checks.
infra-bot: precheck report: sorrel-cutover-precheck at 1719509000 -> warnings: none, infra: NAT IPs reachable, route table present, IAM role arn:arn:aws:iam::999999999999:role/sorrel-provisioner noted. See CI report: https://ci.redwood.ai/reports/sorrel/precheck-1719509000.
cesar_se: one more note on rollback: if CMK access fails during cutover we will failover to a read-only hosted endpoint and pause private DMA. That is a functional degradation; I'll document visibility points in postmortem template.
maya_cs: thanks team. I'll collect feedback after cutover and log any "enablement-gaps" for PS scope. If anything changes, update this thread and I'll escalate to renewal manager if we see >8h unresolved infra gaps.
